requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory.
requirements.summary: The directory was absent initially, then directly observed as root:root with mode 1777. Both antrieb and nobody successfully created files, and the final post-restart observation retained mode 1777 on a writable filesystem.

requirements.requirement: Prevent users from removing files owned by other users in /srv/drop.
requirements.summary: Before and after restart, nobody received “Operation not permitted” when attempting to delete an antrieb-owned file; each file was confirmed to remain present.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: it records a healthy pre-restart directory and data state, restart acknowledgement, observed SSH disruption, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered permissions, data, writability, and sticky-bit behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and setting permissions on /srv/drop directly implemented the task; temporary files supported bounded behavior and restart verification and were removed. The two initial unprivileged creation attempts failed without evidence of changing state. The persistence-check file created by the partially completed probe was reused for the required restart protocol and later cleaned up. The reboot was required provider-wide evidence collection. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services, new listening sockets, package damage, or abandoned verification files.
